trust_decision.summary: The tool trusts the `ref:` value in a downloaded .git/HEAD and joins it onto temp_dst/.git/logs with no segment check, so a malicious .git server picks an arbitrary local path that is probed with os.path.exists and read back; a second, separately-sourced route (HTML listing hrefs through add_folder) reaches the same add_task/worker path-join with only a naive ".."-string strip as protection.

landing_point.why: The summary's 'existence oracle' is exactly this: the server-controlled `.git/HEAD` ref value is joined into `.git/logs/<ref>`, probed with os.path.exists and then read; the same join reappears in worker() at 583-585, so a reader starting from the report lands here first.

fix_sites.entry_point: internal gate called by GitHacker.add_task() and add_folder() (CLI `githacker --url ...`)
GitHacker.start() -> sighted() -> add_folder() (CLI `githacker --url`, Apache/Nginx DirectoryIndex enabled)
GitHacker.add_task() (public method; front door of the download queue for every producer)
worker() thread pool, for every queued download
GitHacker.__init__/start() -> requests session (CLI `--insecure`); unrelated hardening in the same commit (TLS verification default, retries, pool sizing)
GitHacker.__init__ -> complete_basic_files_list() -> parse_current_branch_name() (server response parser); assert replaced by ValueError, robustness rather than the traversal property

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The sighted/directory-listing crawler looks already handled - it strips '..' from the filepath (line 225) and prefix-checks startswith(self.url) 'to prevent CSRF' (lines 222-223) - and the advisory names ref/hash parsing, so a solver can leave the listing route alone as a neighbouring feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Every legitimate download starts with the dot-prefixed `.git` segment (and pack files use dotted/long names); reusing `_is_safe_ref_segment`, which rejects leading dots and `.lock`, as the path gate would block all of them, so an over-broad fix breaks every download while still looking correct.

O6_input_shapes: a multi-segment ref name split on '/' (refs/heads/feature/login)
HTML href values from a directory listing: trailing-slash directory links, '../'/'/' parent links, absolute and cross-origin URLs, percent-encoded names, query-style links
packed-refs lines (sha SP ref) plus '^' peeled lines and comments
wordlist lines that contain '/' and '# ' comments
empty segments, '.', '..', None/non-str, NUL, control characters, backslash, spaces in a segment
a list of components rather than a single string (add_task receives list, not str)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: parse the downloaded `.git/objects/info/alternates` / `http-alternates` files and queue each listed object directory as path segments
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Both files are already downloaded (lines 142-143) but nothing consumes them; reading alternates to recover missing objects is the obvious next recovery feature, and it feeds add_task() exactly like packed-refs does.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second ref source: refs/submodule names taken from the downloaded `.git/config` ([remote] fetch, branch.*.merge) or from `.git/info/refs`, queued the same way packed-refs is
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Packed-refs parsing was added in the pinned commit as a recovery feature; config-driven ref names are the same feature extended, and a maintainer would copy the existing loop.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: queue every href in a listing (including query-string or percent-encoded names) rather than only recursing on directory links
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Apache DirectoryIndex emits '?C=N;O=D' sort links and percent-encoded names, so treating every href as a downloadable path is a plausible tidy-up of the crawler.

O9_family: CWE-22/CWE-23 path traversal - unvalidated server-controlled path segments in ref, hash and file handling

O10_build.toolchain: uv / pip; requires-python >=3.12; deps requests, gitpython, beautifulsoup4, coloredlogs, semver, rich; pytest for tests; Dockerfile = python:3.12-slim + uv sync
services: docker compose + local nginx/apache on 127.0.0.1 for the legacy utils/test.py integration harness
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_ref_validation.py is a pytest suite for _is_safe_ref_segment / _is_safe_sha / _load_ref_wordlist / add_packed_refs_tasks, with no coverage of add_head_file_tasks, add_folder or wget; utils/test.py drives test/docker/*.yml (nginx/apache, DirectoryIndex on/off, http://127.0.0.1/) and no CI workflow runs pytest. Note GitHacker.__init__ itself performs HTTP GETs via parse_current_branch_name/parse_logged_branch_names (lines 406, 420), so offline tests must use GitHacker.__new__ or a stub as the existing tests do.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Gate only the reported oracle: add _is_safe_ref_segment to the .git/HEAD ref path in add_head_file_tasks and stop there, leaving add_task(), add_folder() and URL construction untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: The same fix commit also flips the HTTP client default from verify=False to a verifying requests session with retries and an --insecure flag (CWE-295), which is outside this advisory's path-handling property and was not pursued.
